shadows: none (2 instances in 8000 elements; depth via color-field contrast)

taste.name: Color Is a Chapter Break, Not a Highlighter
taste.trigger: When the designers needed an agency site to feel expressive while showing wildly varied client work
taste.decision: Confined all saturated color (#DFBBFE lavender, #FFB2E8 pink) to full-viewport 1440x900 panels and announcement bars, over threading an accent color through buttons, links, and icons
taste.reason: Client work supplies the site's color; a persistent brand accent would fight every portfolio image. A rare full-screen color flood registers as an event, so announcements feel like news, not chrome

taste.name: Hierarchy by Size Alone, at Poster Scale
taste.trigger: When they had to rank a promise line, section titles, and body copy without cluttering the page
taste.decision: Kept nearly all text at weight 500 in one family and made hierarchy purely with size — 15.33px body to 66.67px h1 to an off-scale 172.45px display — over a conventional weight-and-color hierarchy (bold heads, gray body)
taste.reason: When everything shares one voice and one ink color (#2D2D2D on #EAE8E4), a 4x-11x size jump is unmissable; readers rank content by area, and the page reads like a printed poster rather than a document outline
evidence: weight 500 = 126 of 200 text samples spanning body and h1
h2 switches to Helvetica Now Extended for width-based emphasis

taste.name: Restraint: No Shadows, No Cards, No Gaps
taste.trigger: When they needed to separate dozens of content modules (work, thinking, events, video) on one 8487px page
taste.decision: Rejected the default kit — card containers, elevation shadows, rounded content wrappers, whitespace gaps between sections — in favor of flush full-bleed color fields (#EAE8E4 to #191715) with 113px of internal padding
taste.reason: Boxes-in-boxes make a portfolio feel like a dashboard. Flat color fields joined edge-to-edge feel like turning pages of a printed portfolio, and the background swap tells scrolling readers 'new chapter' faster than any divider line

taste.name: Round Means Clickable
taste.trigger: When links had to stay findable on busy video heroes, pale gray fields, and near-black footers alike
taste.decision: Standardized every interactive element into two shapes — a 100px-radius pill or a 50% circle with an arrow — over color-coded links, underlines, or rectangular buttons
taste.reason: With no accent color available, shape must carry affordance. A circle-with-arrow is recognizable at a glance in any color scheme, so the same component works on dark, light, and lavender surfaces without restyling
evidence: border-radius 100px x106 and 50% x21 vs 4px x11
arrow-circle repeats in nav, feature cards, announcement bar, and 11+ footer policy links
buttons use default case with no letter-spacing
